                             PETITION FOR REVIEW

Rule 15(a) of the Federal Rules of Appellate Procedure, and D.C. Circuit Rule 15,

Sierra Club and the Environmental Law & Policy Center (collectively

Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (“FERC”), as well as any subsequent

amendment or modification of the following orders:

      System Operator, Inc., Order on Complaint, 194 FERC ¶ 61,214, Docket

January 26, 2026 Sierra Club filed a timely motion to intervene. On January 27,

2026 Environmental Law & Policy Center filed an out-of-time motion to intervene,

which was accepted by FERC. See Exhibit A, Order at P 29. On April 20, 2026

                                           ORDER ON COMPLAINT

                                            (Issued March 19, 2026)

                On January 5, 2026, Southern Indiana Gas and Electric Company (SIGE) filed a
         complaint (Complaint) pursuant to sections 202(c), 306, and 309 of the Federal Power
         Act (FPA)1 and Rule 206 of the Commission’s Rules of Practice and Procedure,2
         proposing revisions to the Midcontinent Independent System Operator, Inc. (MISO)
         Open Access Transmission, Energy and Operating Reserve Markets Tariff (Tariff) to add
         a provision (Proposed Tariff Provision) to allocate the costs of keeping Unit 2 of the F.B.
         Culley generating plant (Culley Unit 2) in operation, in response to the U.S. Department
         of Energy’s (DOE) December 23, 2025 Emergency Order No. 202-25-13 (DOE Order),
         under section 202(c) of the FPA and section 301 of the DOE Organization Act.3

                In this order, we grant the Complaint and find that the Proposed Tariff Provision is
         just and reasonable, subject to the outcome of the proceeding in Docket No. ER25-3425.
         We direct MISO to make a compliance filing, within 30 days of the date of a Commission
         order accepting MISO’s compliance filing in Docket No. ER25-3425, to adopt the
         Proposed Tariff Provision, as revised, as discussed below.

         I.     Background

                A.        Culley Unit 2 Retirement Plan

                 Culley Unit 2, located in southwestern Indiana, is a coal-fired unit that has a
         nameplate capacity of 103.7 MW. Culley Unit 2 is owned and operated by SIGE, a
         utility operating subsidiary of CenterPoint Energy, Inc. SIGE planned to retire the unit
         on December 31, 2025, pursuant to commitments SIGE made in a settlement agreement
         approved by the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (Indiana Commission) in 2025.4
         SIGE submitted a notice to suspend operation of Culley Unit 2 to MISO pursuant to
         Attachment Y of the Tariff, and MISO found no reliability violations.

                B.        DOE Order

                 In the DOE Order, the Secretary of Energy determined that “an emergency
         exists in portions of the Midwest region of the United States due to a shortage of electric
         energy, a shortage of facilities for the generation of electric energy, and other causes.”5
         Further, the Secretary of Energy determined that issuance of the DOE Order will “meet
         the emergency and serve the public interest.”6 Therefore, the Secretary of Energy
         directed MISO and SIGE to take all measures necessary to ensure that Culley Unit 2
         is available to operate7 and directed SIGE to keep Culley Unit 2 open for 90 days, i.e.,
         until March 23, 2026.8

                 The DOE Order cited a statement in the 2024 North American Electric Reliability
         Corporation (NERC) Long-Term Reliability Assessment (Reliability Assessment) that
         MISO is at risk because “probabilistic assessments indicate above-normal generator
         outages during extreme weather can result in unserved energy or load loss. With
         uncertainty around new resource additions and existing generator retirements, MISO
         is also at risk of falling below [Reference Margin Levels] within the next five years.”9
         The DOE Order quoted a MISO April 2025 presentation on the Planning Resource

                A.        MISO Answer

                MISO agrees with SIGE that the Tariff does not currently contain a mechanism
         for cost allocation under these circumstances.25 MISO states that it does not oppose
         the Proposed Tariff Provision and that it will file such a schedule if directed by the
         Commission. MISO notes that it reserves the right to change the cost allocation
         mechanism “to account for existing Tariff requirements and to include other clarifications
         as may be appropriate.”26

                B.        Comments and Protests

                 The Michigan Attorney General and the Illinois Commission state that, contrary
         to claims made by the DOE Order, there is no evidence of an energy emergency.27 The
         Illinois Commission asserts that MISO does not need the capacity provided by Culley
         Unit 2 and that MISO has emergency operating procedures, which both belie the notion
         of an emergency in MISO.28 The Illinois Commission further states that the DOE Order
         is an overreach of federal authority because it encroaches on that state’s role in resource
         adequacy and fuel choice.29

                 The Michigan Attorney General opposes the Proposed Tariff Provision, arguing
         that the Commission should reject it because the underlying DOE Order justifying
         cost recovery is ultra vires, and, absent a valid legal obligation to operate pursuant
         to FPA section 202(c), the imposition of the costs of operating Culley Unit 2 on
         ratepayers pursuant to FPA sections 205 or 206 is not just and reasonable and is unduly
         discriminatory or preferential, and violates the filed rate doctrine. Alternatively, the
         Michigan Attorney General requests that the Commission, under the discretion afforded
         the Commission under FPA section 202(c), issue an order deferring any finding, on the
         basis that the Proposed Tariff Provision is premature until the rehearing requests at DOE
         are resolved.30 The Michigan Attorney General also asserts that the Commission should
         limit cost recovery to those costs from the limited scope of operation ordered by the DOE
